name: Garlic
short: Case reports of altered platelet function and clotting, with possible bleeding risk, and of burns from raw garlic on skin. May enhance warfarin; lowered saquinavir levels in a study.
text: In clinical trials the most common complaints were garlic breath and body odour; case reports describe allergic reactions, altered platelet function and coagulation with a possible risk of bleeding, and burns when fresh garlic is applied to the skin, particularly under occlusive dressings. A review of supplements and bleeding found garlic supplementation strongly associated with surgical bleeding independent of anticoagulants, and advised that nonessential supplements be stopped 2 weeks before surgery. Garlic may enhance the effect of anticoagulants such as warfarin and fluindione, and in a study in 10 healthy volunteers garlic supplements lowered blood levels of the HIV medicine saquinavir by about half (51% fall in AUC).
